{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"9d6a7900a8dd481be544ea0029ea66b27e51b702510f43db1bb3ba8930780e6c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Signal lights and arrows, inoperative signals, controlled and uncontrolled intersections, right-of-way and pedestrians","heading":"C — Steady and flashing signal lights, signal arrows, dark signals, T intersections, controlled and uncontrolled intersections, what right-of-way means, yielding to pedestrians and pedestrian-activated signals","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Steady and flashing signal lights, signal arrows, dark signals, T intersections, controlled and uncontrolled intersections, what right-of-way means, yielding to pedestrians and pedestrian-activated signals
Knowledge domain: what each steady and flashing light and arrow requires, how to handle a dark signal or an intersection with no controls, who yields at a T intersection, why the law only says who must yield, and the pedestrian rules and pedestrian-activated signal indications.

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Red, yellow and green signal lights stand at many intersections to control the direction and flow of traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Traffic lights bind pedestrians and bicycle and moped riders as well as motorists. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
You must obey the signal lights unless a police officer directing traffic tells you to do otherwise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
A green light means you may go through the intersection in the direction the signal allows, if the roadway is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Even on green, look left and right for cross traffic before entering, so a red-light runner does not hit you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
On a fresh green, yield to any vehicle that was already in the intersection when the light changed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
On a steady yellow, stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection, but if you are already in it, keep going and clear it safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
Speeding up to beat a yellow light is illegal and could cause a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
On a red light, come to a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk, and stay stopped as long as the light is red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on red after a complete stop once vehicles and pedestrians are clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
The manual's freeway-exit figure shows the correct exit: do not slow down on the freeway itself, slow down in the exit lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop fully, then go on with caution when the way is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution if the roadway is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
A lighted red arrow means you may not turn in its direction; stop and wait for the green signal before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
A yellow arrow is the warning that the arrow signal is about to turn red. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
Facing a yellow arrow, stop and wait for a green arrow if you have not entered the intersection, or finish your turn and clear it safely if you already have. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn with caution after slowing, if the roadway is clear and you first yield to any oncoming vehicle or pedestrian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
A green arrow, alone or with another light, lets you go in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
Treat an intersection whose traffic signal is not working as a 4-way stop: stop completely before entering, then go when the roadway is clear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
When two vehicles reach such an intersection at about the same time, both stop and the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
At a T intersection, the driver on the street that ends must yield to vehicles on the cross street. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A02
At controlled intersections, obey the signals and signs and yield to other vehicles as they direct. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A03
Having the right-of-way does not by itself make it safe to go; check for traffic and pedestrians first. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A03
At a controlled intersection, stop at the stop line. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A03
An intersection with no traffic lights, stop signs or yield signs is treated as a 4-way stop, with a full stop before entering. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A03
The law requires certain vehicles to yield to others; it never actually gives the right-of-way to any driver, it only says who must yield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A03
No one may take the right-of-way if taking it could cause a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A03
You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A03
After your light turns green you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are in the intersection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A03
The law requires a complete stop at any school crossing while anyone is in the crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A03
You may not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian, even if your lane is clear or your signal is green. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A03
For safety, give the right-of-way to anyone you see crossing any street. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A03
At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal, flashing yellow means a pedestrian has pressed the signal, and solid yellow means prepare to stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A03
Solid red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, because a pedestrian is in the crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A03
Flashing red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, then go on with caution after the pedestrian has crossed the driver's half of the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: a green light does not let you go before the intersection is clear of vehicles and pedestrians already in it; a yellow light is not a signal to speed up, beating the light is illegal; at a dark signal with two vehicles arriving together, it is the driver on the left who yields; the law never grants the right-of-way, it only says who must yield.
Mnemonics: Flashing red equals stop sign, flashing yellow equals slow; dark signal means all-way stop, left yields to right.
Glossary: inoperative signal means a traffic light that is dark or not working; T intersection means a junction where one street ends at a cross street; right-of-way means the legal duty of one road user to let another go first; pedestrian-activated signal means a crosswalk signal a pedestrian turns on by pushing a button.
Dynamic facts: signal meanings are stable statute; local signs can forbid a right turn on red at a given intersection, so read the posted signs.
